lines.text: Your phone races to eighty percent... then crawls. That's on purpose.
Charging pushes lithium into tiny layers in the battery. Picture a hotel.
Empty hotel? Guests rush right in. Full power.
But near full, the last guests have to squeeze into the last few rooms.
So the charger stops pushing. It holds the voltage steady, and the current drops.
Forcing it at the top... adds heat and stress. That's what ages batteries.
It's also why an iPhone may wait at eighty overnight, and finish before you wake.
So that slow last twenty percent? Your battery's buying itself a longer life.
